relevance_note: Case series of five children with HA20 and heterozygous TNFAIP3 variants: "We identified five heterozygous variants in the TNFAIP3 gene among the five children".
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; all values were entered from that reading. A Python script (own scratch dir) parsed Tables 1-3 only to build table-row spans and to assert that every hand-entered table value equals its cell; all spans were then checked verbatim against the paper. All three tables have patients as columns: Tables 1 and 2 headers 'Patient 1'...'Patient 5'; Table 3 headers 'Patient 1', 'The case reported by Xue et al', 'Patient 2', 'The case reported by Xue et al', 'Patient 3', 'The case reported by Zhong et al' (with a 'variant site' row merged over each pair). LABELS: the two Table 3 Xue columns share one label, so I appended the variant ('(c.866delA)', '(c.1243_1247delAAAAC)'); 'mother of the case reported by Zhong et al' is a constructed label for the mother named in the text and Table 3 ('Source of variant sites ... mother'). Previously published people summarised in the Discussion are included as their own rows (ref-32 infant with a 187 kb microdeletion; Harumi et al. adult-onset patient; Zhong case's mother); the L Lin et al. (46) HA20+MMA case and aggregate cohorts (systematic review ref 14, Chen's study) were not given rows (no individual detail). CONTRADICTIONS: (1) MMACHC variants c.349G>C: p.A117P and c.482G>A: p.R161Q are attributed to patient 3 in the Abstract and Discussion but to patient 2 in the Figure 1 (C, D) legend, and the MMA diagnosis/hydroxocobalamin is stated for patient 2 in Treatment and follow-up; MMACHC variants omitted, MMA recorded only for Patient 2 where explicitly stated. (2) The Table 3 column headed 'Patient 3' carries c.133C>T: p. R45X (Patient 4's variant in Table 1 and text) and phenotypes matching Patient 4, but treatment 'Thalidomide, glucocorticoid' matching Patient 3 (Table 1 gives Patient 4 'Thalidomide'); that column was not used for anyone. (3) Patient 2 oral ulcers: Table 1 and Table 3 'NO' vs Discussion 'patient 2 had rash, gastrointestinal ulcers, and oral ulcers'; both rows emitted, checklist 'not reported'. (4) Discussion gives gastrointestinal ulcers 80% while Table 1 lists gastrointestinal lesions YES for all five and endoscopy describes ulcers in all five (Abstract counts of oral ulcers 3/5 match Table 1, not the Discussion). (5) Xue et al c.1243_1247delAAAAC case: text 'no liver injury' but Table 3 ALT 165.6 and AST 172.9 (reference 0~40); recorded 'no liver injury' as excluded and did not turn the ALT/AST numbers into features. (6) Text says Xue 'patients with the same mutation' (plural) where Table 3 shows one case per variant; one row each. (7) Discussion onset ages equal the Table 1 ages at genetic diagnosis for patients 2 and 5; recorded as stated. (8) 'All patients aged from 2 to 10 years' conflicts with Table 1 diagnosis ages (6m to 5y8m) and is unclear which age; not recorded. OTHER CHOICES: Table 1 row 'Genomic location (GRCh37/ hg19)' holds c./p. strings; GRCh37 recorded only for Patient 3's NC_000006.11 g. deletion. Transcript NM_006290.5 (Table 1 note) applied only to Patients 1, 2, 4, 5 c. variants, not to literature cases or the g. deletion. 'frameshift' for the three variants the authors call 'small indels' rests on their 'fs' protein notation. 'de novo' for Patients 1-5 rests on 'they have all been tested to confirm their origin'; Table 3 'de novo' for both Xue cases and '187 kb de novo microdeletion' (ref 32) were left inheritance 'not reported' under rule 8 (no parental-testing statement for those people). 'Arthritis NO' did not exclude 'arthritis or arthralgia'; motor and cognitive developmental delay was not mapped to CNS involvement or growth failure; 'no liver injury' was not used to exclude autoimmune hepatitis; low hemoglobin (attributed by the authors to inflammation) was not mapped to autoimmune cytopenia. Elevated CRP/ESR, low hemoglobin and diarrhea rest on 'all five'/'all patients' statements plus Table 2 values; marked 'inferred from group statement' unless the patient is named (CRP cases 2, 3, 4; ESR cases 1, 3, 5). WBC, platelet and IL-6 values not turned into features. Table 3 'Gastrointestinal lesions NO' taken as excluding 'gastrointestinal ulcers or inflammation' for the Zhong case. is_proband left null for Patients 1-5 (paper never uses 'proband'/'index'). The paper presents the Xue et al cases as different people from Patients 1 and 2 (different phenotypes and treatments). Some Table 3 row-prefix spans also occur verbatim in Table 1. Figure 1 legend prints the CNV as 'NC000006.11: g.136693638138817508del' (typographic variant).
